title: [Beta] AI Graphic Generator (Ver. 2024.1)
content: ### ### ### Objective Easily type in keywords to generate different graphic images to choose from to create new graphics. ### Location Graphic Property ▶ Material ▶ Basic Parameters ▶**![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341773977)**AI Graphic Generator button ### Operation 1. Create a pattern piece to place a graphic on. 2. Add a graphic to the pattern using the add [Graphic (2D Pattern) Tool](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358239678745) 3. Select the Graphic in the 2D window. 4. Under Graphic Properties ▶**![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438341773977)**AI Graphic Generator button to the right of the Basic Parameters → AI Graphic Generator window appears. 5. Set Content Type, Transparent Background, enter prompts and click the Generate button. 6. Check the generated graphic in the preview window. → The generated graphic is stored in History. 7. Click generate again to generate more Graphic images. 8. Click Apply button, the selected image is applied as the Graphic. #### **Generate AI Graphic Options** Content Type | Select the type of content for the graphic to be generated. ---|--- None | Create an image without specifying characteristics of the graphic image. Art | Set the characteristics of the graphic image: * Embroidery, Patch, Pop Art Transparent Background | Apply a transparent background to the image. ※ Note: This option is not available for the Pop Art type. Text Prompt | Enter the prompt. **✨ Writing Tips:** * **List words.** * Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. * **Emphasize certain words more than others.** * * If parentheses are used in the word you want to emphasize, it takes up more weight. Parentheses on certain words take more weight. Weight increase rate: **(word)** 1.1 times, **((word))** 1.21 times. ![Frame 247.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438325431449) **![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358161481369)**Maintain Prompt | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Graphic image is newly created each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while maintaining the characteristics of the previously generated result as much as possible. ※ Note: It may differ from the existing results depending on the addition or change of the prompts. **![icon_random_dice.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358161483545)**Random | The sample prompt is randomly applied. This option automatically changes to a type specific to the prompt. #### History | Previously generated images with prompts are recorded as "histories". The history remains accessible until Marvelous Designer is closed. If you select a previously created image in History and click Apply, the image is applied as Texture. ※ Note: * It may take a while to create when there are many users generating AI graphic images at the same time. * The resulting generated images are only a preview until Apply is selected.
content_description: "Quickly generate and customize unique graphic images by entering keywords and utilizing our AI Graphic Generator tool."

title: Avatar Friction Setting
content: ### Objective Increase avatar friction to prevent the garment from sliding off during draping or animation. ※ Note: Adjusting the friction between the avatars and garments or between the garments allows desired draping direction. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Static/Kinetic Friction Coefficient ※ Note: Static Friction Coefficient | Friction Coefficient between avatars and garments when the garment is fixed. ---|--- Kinetic Friction Coefficient | Friction Coefficient between avatars and garments when garments are movable. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Static/Kinetic Friction Coefficient 2. Enter a desired value of Static or Kinetic Friction Coefficient. 3. Click Simulate to simulate according to the set value.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting avatar friction settings to enhance garment stability during draping and animation.

title: Pose (*.pos) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Use this function to load an Avatar’s Pose or location information. If a Pose file is loaded the Simulation button is automatically turned on and the Avatar gradually changes from the current Pose to the new Pose. The Garments worn by the Avatar are also simulated. ### Location #### Open Pose (Change) Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Pose (Ctrl+Shift+P) #### Save Pose Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Pose ### Operation #### Open Pose (Change) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Pose (Ctrl+Shift+P) → The Simulation automatically turns on and the Avatar's Pose changes. 2. While the Pose is being changed, the Play Motion tool or Simulation tool can be clicked to stop the Pose. 3. Click Play Motion tool or Simulation tool to restart the pose change. #### Save Pose 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Pose → The Save File window appears. 2. Type in the file name and designate the path the file is saved to. 3. Select Save. → The Pose (*.pos) file is saved. #### Open/Load Hand Pose (ver.2024.1) 1. Load an avatar into the scene. 2. Load hand pose file (.hpos) or Pose file (.pos) 3. In the Open Pose dialog box select the type of Joint Information ▶ Partial Pose (Both Hands, Left Hand, or Right Hand). 4. Click OK button. → The pose is applied to selected hands only. ※ Note: * The (.hpos) file is a format that deals only with the hand pose. * The hand pose can be applied among all poses through the .pos file. * The (.hpos) is provided as downloadable content in the Library (ver.2024.1). The library (.hpos) files only apply to Female_V2 and Male_V2 avatar types. #### Load Pose Type When importing a Pose with joints differing from the original Avatar, the Pose type can be set like below: Avatar Size + Joint Rotation & Position (Ver. 10) | Applies the Avatar's Size, Pose, Motion Data (joint rotation) and Joint positions. ---|--- Joint Rotation Only (Ver. 10) | Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Cancel or re-load Avatars using the Ctrl + Z, Ctrl + Y keys (ver5.0.0.) #### Open Pose Dialogue Box (ver. 2024.1) Pose Only (Maintain Avatar Size) | Applies the Avatar's Size, Pose, Motion Data (joint rotation) and Joint positions. ---|--- Pose & Joint Translation | Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Partial Pose | Full Body | Apply Pose file to full body. Both Hands | Apply Partial Pose file to both hands. Left hand | Apply Partial Pose file to left hand only. Right hand | Apply Partial Pose file to right hand only. Maintain Current Shoe Pose | Maintains shoe pose while applying additional pose information. Align Bottom to ground | Align bottom of avatar to ground after applying pose information. Reset | While the dialog box is running, reset settings to default Apply | Apply pose based on the input values entered. Cancel | Close the dialog box without applying ※ Note: If a Pose file is loaded, the simulation is automatically turned on and the avatar changes from the current Pose to the new Pose. ### End Result Avatar's pose (.pos) file and hand pose (.hpos) file is applied, and avatar change to the applied pose.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for loading and saving Avatar poses and hand poses, enabling seamless transitions and simulations of avatar movements and garment behaviors.

title: Copy/Paste Patterns (3D)
content: ### Objective Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window. ### Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Copy or Paste ### Operation 1. Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Copy or Paste → A preview of the copied pattern follows the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the desired location in the 3D window to place the duplicated pattern. → The copied pattern is automatically assigned a number. ※ Note: * To copy and paste more efficiently, select the pattern, press Ctrl+C, then press Ctrl+V or Ctrl+R on the keyboard to copy, paste or mirror paste, respectively. * Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window to another Marvelous Designer software window (ver3.0.0). This is only available in Windows.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for efficiently copying and pasting patterns within the 3D window of Marvelous Designer software.

title: Create Additional Fabric
content: ### Objective Create additional Fabric styles. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Add ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Add → A new Fabric item is now being added to the Fabric list. 2. Drag and drop a Fabric file (.ZFAB / .XTEX) onto the Fabric list in the Object Browser. → The selected Fabric file is now being added to the list. ※ Note: * Drag and drop a Fabric file onto an existing style replaces its properties. * Default_Fabric is provided as default fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until rerun of the program. It is able to reset edited properties of Default_Fabric at right-click pop-up menu but it is indelible.

title: Avatar/ Joints Right-Click Menu
content: ### ### Objective Options and functions to modify Avatar Joints. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Right-click Pop-up Menu on the Avatar or Joint of avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below to access Joints Right Click Menu: 3D Window ▶ Right-click Pop-up Menu on the Avatar or Joint of avatar ### #### Avatar Option Menu Select All Faces | Select all avatar faces bind to the root of the joint selected. ---|--- Delete Avatar | Delete the avatar bind to the root of the joint selected. Delete All Avatars | Delete all avatars in the scene. Delete Scene and Prop | Delete selected scene and props. Delete All Scene and Prop | Delete all scene and props in the scene. Move Avatar | To Center | Move the avatar bind to the root of the joint selected to the center of 3D window. To Ground | Move the avatar bind to the root of the joint selected to the ground plane. Move All Avatars & Garments | To Center | Move All Avatars and Garments to the center of 3D window. To Ground | Move All Avatars and Garments to the ground plane. Reset Joints (Ver. 2.3.0) | Reset avatar's joints back to default transformation settings. Hide Joint (Ver. 2024.2) | Hide selected joint/joints. in the 3D window. Show All Joints (Ver. 2024.2) | Show All Joints in the 3D window. Change Heels | Up | Change rotation of Heels joints to Up preset. Down | Change rotation of Heels joints to Down preset. Activate Avatar | Activate selected avatar. Hide Avatar | Hide selected avatar in the 3D window. Hide All Avatars | Hide all avatars in the 3D window. Refresh Textures | Refresh selected avatar textures. Export to USD Layer | Export selected avatar to USD authoring layer, or create a new USD file with the selected trims. \- To learn more on USD export and USD layer editor in Marvelous Designer. Please move to [USD file Compatibility](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358343098777) page.

title: Show Simulation Speed (Below ver.12.1)
content: ### Objective Check Simulation Speed of CLO on device in use. Recommended Simulation Speed for running CLO is between 25 and 30 FPS when simulating the pre-loaded default garment. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Frame Rate ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Frame Rate → The Simulation Speed displays at the bottom-left corner of the 3D window. ※ Note: The Simulation Speed is measured when the simulation is on. The higher the value of FPS (Frames per Second), the faster the simulation speed.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for checking the simulation speed of CLO on your device, ensuring optimal performance between 25 and 30 FPS while using the pre-loaded default garment.

title: 3D 1:N Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Segment Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. 5. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. 6. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. ※ Note * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for sewing multiple segments to a single segment using the 3D window, ensuring accurate alignment and efficient workflow.

title: Tack on Avatar
content: ### Objective Temporarily fix a point of a Garment to an Avatar. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack on Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Tack on Avatar 2. Click on a point of a 3D Garment to fix. → A point is now being created and a dotted line follows along the mouse cursor, and the selected garment becomes semi-transparent. 3. Click on a point of an Avatar. → The selected Garment is now being opaque once again. → Same tack is now being created in the corresponding 2D Pattern. 4. Activate Simulate. → The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to the Avatar.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for temporarily fixing a garment to an avatar using the tack feature in a 3D design environment.

title: Motion (*.mtn) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Motion is a native file format (*mtn) of Marvelous Designer that saves Avatar movement information, and is used when recording Animation of Garments and Avatars. Marvelous Designer provides Motion files for its default male and female Avatars, but Animation Data or Motion capture Data from third-party 3D solutions can be imported as COLLADA files, then extracted as a Motion file (*mtn) through this menu. ### Location #### Open Motion Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Joint Motion #### Save Motion Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Joint Motion ### Operation #### Open Motion 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Joint Motion → The Open File window appears. 2. Navigate to the desired *mtn file, then click Open. → The Load Motion Type window appears. 3. Select from the available settings: Joint Information | Joint Rotation & Translation | Applies the Avatar's Height, Pose, Motion Data (Joint rotation,) and Joint positions ---|---|--- Joint Rotation Only | Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. Garment Position | Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver 2.5.0). Transition Animation | A transition Animation is an Animation that changes from a T-Pose to a motion's first Pose in stages, and is created when the Avatar's current Pose and Motion differs from that of the first frame Pose. → The motion (*mtn) file loads according to the settings. #### Save Motion 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Joint Motion → The Save File window appears. 2. Type in file name and designate the path the file will be saved to. → The Motion (*mtn) file will be saved to the designated path. ※ Note: * Motion files can only be saved when imported as Avatars in COLLADA format with Motion Data, and the COLLADA files must be in Open COLLADA format. * To learn more about COLLADA format, please reference [3D File (COLLADA) Import](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358302910361). * The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to open and save Objective Motion (*mtn) files in Marvelous Designer, detailing the process for importing motion data and customizing avatar animations.

title: Create 2D Measurements
content: ### Internal Shape ### Objective View the position of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. To Outline View | the 2D Measurements from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Shape to the Pattern outline. ---|--- To Center View | the 2D Measurements from the center of the Internal Shape to the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline. →2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. ### Internal Line ### Objective View the position of Internal Lines or segments of Internal Shapes from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. → 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items. ### Internal Point ### Objective View the position of internal points or internal curve points from the Pattern outline with 2D Measurements (ver2.5.0). ### Location Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Center ### Operation 1. 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern Tool ▶ Select the Internal Shape/Dart. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ 2D Measurements ▶ To Outline/To Center 3. Select the desired 2D Measurements to display. → 2D Measurements appear based on the selected items.

Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Pattern Window ▶ Edit Texture(2D)▶ Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu ▶ Reset to Basic Fabric Object Browser ▶ Right-click Fabric List Pop-up Menu ▶ Reset →The selected Fabric's texture, color and physical properties are now being reset.

title: Select/Move Point/Segment
content: ### ### ### Objective Modify Patterns and Internal Shapes by moving points and segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Select 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Click a point or segment of a Pattern or Internal Shape. → The point or segment is selected. → When there are multiple points or segments, a pop-up menu appears allowing you to select the desired one (ver3.0.0.) 3. To select multiple points and segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard when clicking them. → All clicked points and segments are selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass points and segments to be selected with the marquee box. → All points and segments inside the marquee box are selected. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ TEdit Pattern 2. Click and drag the Pattern or use the arrow keys. 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the point or segment. → The point or segment can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the point or segment to type in distance moved. Option | Description ---|--- Distance Moved | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. X-Axis (ver4.2.0) | Type in how much a point is moved on x-axis. This option does not appear for segments. Y-Axis (ver4.2.0) | Type in how much a point is moved on Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments. ※ Note: If it is cumbersome to select Patterns using the Edit Pattern tool, use the Transform Pattern tool.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for modifying patterns and internal shapes by selecting and moving points and segments within a 2D editing interface.

title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
content: ### Objective Write and check important Garment information. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ Garment ### Operation #### Enter Default Garment Information 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶ Garment → The Garment Information window appears. 2. Click the Edit icon on the right top corner of the window. → The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. 3. Type in necessary information next to each category and click OK. → Typed in information is saved. #### Add Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the Add icon. → A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. → There are eight categories to choose from: Code, Name, Description, Price, Fabric, Size, Colorway, Category, and Memo. 3. Type in necessary information for each category and click OK. → Typed in information is saved. #### Reorder Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click and drag the category to the desired position. → The category is moved to where the mouse is released. 3. When categories are re-ordered completely, click OK. → Revised category order is saved. #### Delete Category 1. Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. 2. Click the Delete icon next to each category. → The selected category is deleted. 3. When the editing is completed, click OK. → The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. ※ Note: * Toggle on Display When Garment File Loads option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. * Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the Open and Save buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. * Use the Default File setting to designate default Garment Information file.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for users to enter, edit, add, reorder, and delete garment information efficiently within the application.

title: Wind Controller Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust and apply wind effect to create fluttering effect on garment in the 3D window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller ### Operation #### Activate Wind Effect 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. ![11.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438677359257) 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3\. Wind ▶ Toggle on (Check Box) at Activate. → It is now being activated (Toggled On) and becomes in blue color. ![22.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438687951001) 4\. Click Simulation. → The Wind Effect is now being activated in the 3D window. #### Wind Direction Setting 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. ![33.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688142617) 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller Gizmo activates. 3\. Use the Gizmo to set direction and location of the wind. 4\. Click Simulation. → The Wind Effect is now being activated as adjusted in the 3D window. #### Wind Properties Setting 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Show Wind Controller → Cone-shaped Wind Controller appears in the 3D window. 2\. Click the Wind Controller. → Wind Controller properties appear in the Property Editor. 3\. Adjust the default values at Property Editor according to the needs. Name | Changes name of the wind according to the user preference. ---|--- Wind | Activate | Sets the activation status of the wind. Type | Sets the type of the wind. Spherical: The wind blows in spherical shape, in every direction starting from the Wind Controller. ![44.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688303641) Planar: The wind blows only from the designated direction, regardless of the Wind Controller's location. ![55.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438688411929) Strength | Sets the intensity of the wind. The higher the value, the stronger the wind. Decay [0~100] | Sets the range of the wind. The wind draws an arc and blows weaker according to the set value of wind intensity. If the value is "0", it blows in a straight line endlessly. Frequency (sec) | Sets the cycle of the wind. The wind repeatably blows weaker and stronger in interval of set value of seconds. If the value is "0", it blows regularly. Turbulence [0~100] | Sets the turbulence of wind intensity. The higher the value, the more irregular the wind intensity.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for activating and customizing wind effects in a 3D environment to create a realistic fluttering effect on garments.

title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
content: ### Objective This function allows easier simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons, gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dress and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is being off. In that state, the arrangement order of the patterns gets decided. ### Location Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Layer ### Operation 1. Select a pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with Select/Move tool. ※ Note: Select patterns in the 2D window, in case of having difficulties when choosing in the 3D window. 2. Follow the guide below: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Layer 3. Apply the value by clicking Simulate button. ※Note: * When the layer value is being set, the patterns become highlighted in blue outline. Once the draping in desired order is completed, set the value back to zero ('0') for more stable simulation. (There is no change in draping even after modifying the value back to zero('0')). If the layer value is zero('0'), but the menu appears in red when all patterns are being selected, it is because there is a variety of values being mixed. Therefore revert the layer value to zero('0') once again. * Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu ▶ Show/Hide Color [(Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358311619225)[ ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/32523191112473/preview/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6MzI1MjMxOTExMTI0NzMsImV4cCI6MTcxNTk3NDk0Mn0.vTz8AEFpwglRHaNeFb09thKYnyuNna7SAvTfH7sSS8U)to hide the layered patterns outline highlight color in the 3D window. ## Show layer Depth (Ver. 2024.1) ### Objective Toggle view option in the 2D window to display the layer number and color code to help visualize layers. ### ### Location 2D Window ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439322905)2D Information ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer ### Operation 1. Follow the guideline for Apply Layer Value to number different pattern layers: 2. Select and enter desired Layer number on selected pattern or multiple patterns. →Layer value is assigned 3. Set different layer values for other patterns. 4. Click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer option under ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439322905)2D information icon to activate. → Number of layer will be indicated and patterns with the same layer will be the same color 5. Click the ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438501035801)Show Pattern Layer option again to inactivate it. ※ Note: * The color values for each layer are as follows. * Layer 0 has one unique color: Light Gray * Layers 1 to 23 each have different color values. This repeats from 24 onwards. * ![image-20240415-003712.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438439968665) * Negative Layers are applied in the reverse order of positive numbers. * Layer depth display will automatically turn off when switching to another [2D Pattern Rendering Style](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358205499033). ### End Result Quickly visualizing and controlling layers is now convenient and intuitive
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the layer simulation function to easily manage overlapping garment patterns, ensuring accurate draping and visual representation in both 2D and 3D views.

title: Button Property Setting
content: ### Objective Adjust button properties in the Property Editor. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Explanation Selecting a button with Select/Move or Select/Move Button tool displays its properties in the Property Editor. Button Property | Description ---|--- Angle | Enter desired value for rotation angle of buttons. Thread Length (cm) | Enter desired value for thread length in centimeter (cm) from the range of 0.00~1.00. Style | Select a button style. Collision | Set ON/OFF for collision option. → Set it OFF in order to fix its location to avoid the collision between the buttons and the Patterns. 2D Measurements | View the position of buttons in 2D Pattern with its size measurement. Set check-boxes On for Left/Right/Up/Down as desired. → The 2D size measurements appear accordingly. Polygon Optimization | Count | Set the number of polygons. ---|---|--- Plane | This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting button properties using the Property Editor, including settings for angle, thread length, style, collision options, 2D measurements, and polygon optimization.
